subject: Commercial: Bridge credits & smoothing pool proposal (Civitas RFP)
messages:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
To: Dirk Muller <dirk.muller@civitashealth.com>, Procurement Team <procurement@civitashealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sat, 21 Aug 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Commercial framework for Civitas RFP — bridge credits + smoothing pool

Dirk / Procurement Team,

Thanks again for the productive call this morning. Attached is our proposed commercial framework tailored to Civitas's ask for predictable unit economics while preserving operational burst capacity. High level summary: 

- Commit ladder: 3-tier 12-month commit (Base / Growth / Scale) with discrete per-token rates.
- Bridge credits: one-time pool of committed credits usable during ramp months to avoid immediate overages. Credits paid upfront with simple amortization.
- Smoothing pool: monthly smoothing allowance (5% of committed tokens) to absorb short-term spikes without overage charges; true-up quarterly.
- Burst resilience: temporary burst cap (2x committed monthly run-rate) with excess billed at an overage rate that declines with higher commit tiers.
- Metering: separate metering for chat generation, embeddings, and reranking; example price matrix attached.

I've included a short attachment (Civitas_RFP_Commercial_Framework_v1.pdf) and a link to a working HubSpot deal. If this structure looks compatible we can generate a detailed pricing table and sample blended-rate calculations for your finance team.

Next steps: please confirm whether Civitas requires: (1) prepaid bridge credits, (2) invoice cadence (monthly vs. quarterly), and (3) any legal/PO workflow constraints so we can scope the SOW.

Best,
Sean Gallagher
Sr. Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Attachment: Civitas_RFP_Commercial_Framework_v1.pdf (PDF, 2 pages)

From: Dirk Muller <dirk.muller@civitashealth.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@civitashealth.com>, Civitas Legal <legal@civitashealth.com>
Date: Sun, 22 Aug 2027 10:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Commercial framework for Civitas RFP — bridge credits + smoothing pool

Sean — thanks for the summary and quick turnaround. A few clarifying items from our side: 

1) We like the idea of a smoothing pool but need a clearer example of how it behaves across a sudden 3-week spike. Will credits apply first, then smoothing, then overage?
2) Bridge credits: Procurement generally prefers a modest upfront payment capped at Q1 usage; would Redwood consider amortizing bridge credits over the first 6 months?
3) Burst cap: civitas wants to ensure critical peaks (e.g., end-of-quarter reporting) are covered without a punitive overage. Can you show a 30% higher burst cushion for the first 3 months?
4) Metering: we bill back internally by model class — please confirm that embeddings are metered separately and priced per-embedding unit.

Legal: we have to review SOW language around data retention and audit logging; can Redwood include standard SOC2 evidence language in the contract appendix?

If you can send detailed calc examples and a 1-page table showing blended rates at three commit levels, we can take this to finance next week.

Thanks,
Dirk
Dirk Muller
Head of Cloud Ops
Civitas Health

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Dirk Muller <dirk.muller@civitashealth.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 23 Aug 2027 08:17:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Commercial framework for Civitas RFP — bridge credits + smoothing pool

Dirk — appreciate the specific asks. Below is an operationalized proposal that addresses each point; I've attached a working pricing workbook (pricing_table_civitas.xlsx). Key changes from Sean's note: 

- Order of consumption: 1) Bridge credits (if available), 2) Smoothing pool allowance, 3) Committed monthly allocation, 4) Overage at published overage rate. This ensures bridge credits and smoothing are protective during ramp/spikes.
- Bridge amortization: we can amortize upfront bridge credits over the first 6 months for Civitas to smooth cashflow; remaining credits expire at month 12.
- Burst cushion: propose a temporary +30% burst envelope for months 1–3 with a capped overage discount schedule (first 10% over cap at 50% of published overage, next 20% at 75%).
- Metering: confirmed — embeddings billed per-embedding unit; generation (chat) billed per-token. Reranking billed at per-request unit (see workbook).

Pricing matrix highlights (examples only — see workbook):
- Base commit (250M tokens/month): chat $0.0035/token, embeddings $0.0010/embedding, rerank $0.015/req
- Growth commit (750M tokens/month): chat $0.0028/token, embeddings $0.00085/embedding, rerank $0.012/req
- Scale commit (2B tokens/month): chat $0.0020/token, embeddings $0.0007/embedding, rerank $0.009/req

We included a "blended effective rate" sheet in the workbook showing blended $/token at representative workload mixes (70% chat, 20% embeddings, 10% rerank) and examples of 3-month spike scenarios.

Ask: Dirk — if Civitas is comfortable with the amortization approach and the pierce-through order of consumption, we'll produce a clean SOW and sample invoice schedule for review.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive
Redwood Inference

Attachment: pricing_table_civitas.xlsx (Excel, 1 sheet)

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Dirk Muller <dirk.muller@civitashealth.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 24 Aug 2027 15:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Commercial framework for Civitas RFP — bridge credits + smoothing pool

Dirk/Team — I pulled together three worked examples to show the net effect of the amortized bridge credits and smoothing pool (attached calc_examples.csv). Short summary: 

Example A — Ramp month (50% of committed run-rate):
- Committed monthly allocation: 500M tokens
- Actual usage: 750M tokens (50% spike)
- Bridge credits applied first: 100M tokens
- Smoothing pool (5% of committed = 25M) applied next
- Remaining 625M consumed against committed -> no overage for remainder
- Net effective blended chat $/token (70/20/10 mix): $0.00265

Example B — Acute 3-week spike (250% of month baseline):
- Burst cushion covers first 2x committed; remaining excess billed at overage schedule (discounted tiers as Marissa described).
- Net blended rate increases but remains below the immediate pay-as-you-go list price thanks to amortized bridge credits.

Notes on billing: we can invoice bridge credits upfront or as a 6-month amortization schedule (monthly invoices). For compliance, Laura: please confirm if we need the SOC2 evidence language included in the pricing appendix or if that should stay in the security addendum.

Regards,
Ben Carter
Pricing & Commercial Ops
Redwood Inference

Attachment: calc_examples.csv (CSV, 3 rows)

From: Dirk Muller <dirk.muller@civitashealth.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@civitashealth.com>, Civitas Legal <legal@civitashealth.com>
Date: Wed, 25 Aug 2027 14:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Commercial framework for Civitas RFP — bridge credits + smoothing pool

Team — this is helpful, thank you. Civitas finance is comfortable with the 6-month amortization for bridge credits and the proposed order of consumption. We also like the temporary +30% burst for months 1–3. Two final asks before we route to legal: 

1) Please prepare a 1-page SOW addendum that captures: commit tiers, bridge credit amount and amortization schedule, smoothing pool size, burst window and overage tiers.
2) Please include a short security appendix referencing SOC2 Type II with a pointer to evidence (or confirm that evidence will be provided under NDA).

If you can share a DocuSign-ready SOW and indicate expected invoice cadence (monthly amortization recommended), we can circulate to Legal and Procurement for signatures next week.

Once we have the signed SOW we'll set up a kickoff and capacity planning call.

Thanks,
Dirk
